output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mainly an inside-the-DC problem, not a Haverlow problem. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four in week 31, chilled pallets wait a median of about 3 h 52 min on the unrefrigerated dock (previously 44 min). The dock averages 15–17°C overnight. Night-shift write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, Haverlow, Pellridge and own-label alike, while day-shift rates stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open. The warm receiving readings are taken after the long dock wait, so they don't show what arrived. The chambers are holding temperature. The chargeback and volume move would punish the wrong party, so don't do them. Instead, restore night receiving staffing, or otherwise fix dock-to-chamber time, and set a maximum time monitored weekly. Probe pallets at unload, not at confirmation. Dropping the night probe would hide the problem. Separately, Corriebank's rise in credits started when self-certification began, but that rise may also be partly real spoilage from the warm dock. Pull a sample of claims and reconcile them before changing credit terms. I'm fairly confident in the main cause. The Corriebank share is unresolved.
